classification.difficultyReason: This is the same two-elevation, perpendicular-direction structure as p14-q1, but the triangle scaffolds are removed. The student must complete the partly supplied diagram and see that north and west give a right angle at the pole's foot. They then find two ground distances with tan and combine them by Pythagoras. The right angle is stated through the compass directions rather than needing bearing reasoning. There is no show-that step or separate elevation sub-question as in p15-q5, so the demand sits just above p14-q1 and below p15-q5.

classification.difficultyReason: The method is the same as p16-q8: two tan ratios for the ground legs, then Pythagoras on the right angle between due north and due east. Here the student must also draw the 3D diagram from scratch, which adds a representation change that p14-q1 and p16-q8 partly supply. The calculation is still a single routine chain with no hidden insight. It sits slightly above p16-q8 and above p14-q1, but below p15-q5, which needs a derived expression and a further elevation angle.
